core_capabilities.description: Single-document parse of a Core mapping, scalar, or sequence, including `answer: 42` as a numeric 42 and ignoring a leading byte-order mark
Multi-document parse returns documents in order, two empty document-start markers as two nulls, and empty or comment-only text as an empty list
Distinguish the two parse entries on empty input and on a multi-document stream: single-document fails, multi-document succeeds
Anchors and aliases share constructed identity, including a recursive alias on the default sequence and mapping tags
Reject duplicate keys by default; with JSON-parse compatibility the later pair wins on every document of the stream

Decode double-quoted and single-quoted folding (CR/LF as space; backslash-joined breaks only in double quotes), eight-digit Unicode escapes, and `%TAG` handles that contain digits (`%TAG !a1! tag:yaml.org,2002:` then `--- !a1!str 123` is the string `123`)

Reject unknown explicit tags, explicit tags on the wrong node kind, and the documented malformed inputs (including unpaired UTF-16 surrogate code units U+DC00 followed by U+D800), yielding no usable document

When a source-path label is supplied, include that label in the failure report and present line-break count one for `a: 1` then CR/LF then `@` versus count zero for `@` then CR/LF then `a: 1` (a CR/LF pair is one break; the count is not a byte offset, a column, or a parse-step; storage, print form, and zero- versus one-based numbering are not scored)
Failsafe keeps plain scalars as strings while still constructing sequences and mappings
JSON implicit null, boolean, integer, and float rules, including the documented forms that stay strings
Core (the parse default) implicit null, boolean, integer, and float rules, including forms that stay strings and overflow `1e999`

YAML 1.1 implicit boolean, integer, and float notations, including sexagesimal and underscores, without treating YAML 1.2 `0o` as an integer (implicit `0o123` stays a string; explicit `!!int 0o123` fails)

Explicit tags resolve or fail independently of implicit rules: empty `!!str`/`!!seq`/`!!map`, shared numeric forms across typed schemas, a decimal integer that is `1` followed by 399 zeros staying a string on JSON/Core/YAML 1.1, and rejected `!!bool`/`!!int`/`!!float` text
Schema selection is the only switch for these implicit rules; Core must not apply YAML 1.1 sexagesimal, underscore, leading-zero-octal, or yes/on boolean words
Default plain-object map stores string properties, stringifies non-string scalar keys, and keeps `__proto__` as an own data property without prototype pollution
Default plain-object map rejects a sequence or mapping used as a key
Real-map replacement constructs a `Map` that keeps numeric keys distinct from string keys and preserves complex keys through dump-then-parse
Legacy-map replacement stringifies sequence and mapping keys, still stores `__proto__` as an own property, and rejects a nested-array key (including via alias)
Attaching the real-map or legacy-map tag replaces the default `!!map` for that schema rather than offering three simultaneous containers
`!!binary` constructs a `Uint8Array` from Base64, dump-then-parse restores the bytes, an empty `!!binary` is an empty `Uint8Array`, and invalid Base64 fails

`!!timestamp` implicit UTC forms construct date values, one-digit months stay strings, impossible calendar values stay strings implicitly and fail when explicit, and dump-then-parse restores the instant
`!!set` constructs a `Set` of keys with null values, dumps with `!!set`, and rejects a non-null set item
`!!omap` constructs an ordered sequence of single-key mappings with unique keys, is load-only on dump, and rejects mapping-shaped or multi-key items
`!!pairs` constructs an array of two-element arrays, allows duplicate keys, rejects complex keys on the default map, and preserves them on real-map

Merge keys are off under Core and on under YAML 1.1 or Core with the merge tag; an explicit pair wins over a merged pair; a later mapping in a merge sequence does not overwrite a key already brought in by an earlier mapping (`<<: [ { r: 10 }, { r: 1 } ]` yields `r: 10`); illegal merge sources fail
Dump-then-parse of `{ answer: 42 }` restores numeric 42; the default dump schema quotes YAML 1.1 boolean words (`yes`, `Yes`, `on`, …) and `true`/`42`/`null`; under JSON the string `yes` is plain
Quote strings that would be read as YAML structure (`---`, `--- x`, `...`, `- value`, `=`, `foo: bar`) and strings that begin or end with a space, while leaving `---x` and `...x` plain
Honor quote style (single vs double) and the quote-every-non-key-string switch
Dump integers at or above `1e21` as floats and round-trip special floats (NaN, infinities, small exponents) on JSON, Core, and YAML 1.1

Reuse a second occurrence of the same object as an alias by default, and inline both copies when the no-reuse switch is on; when a node has both an anchor and an explicit tag, default order is anchor then tag, and a switch reverses that to tag then anchor
Apply indent width, line width, sequence-indent, nested-sequence, flow-depth, and flow-presentation choices as documented
Sort keys when a comparator-less sort is requested; otherwise keep insertion order
Fail dump of functions and regular expressions unless the skip-unrepresentable switch is on; treat `undefined` as documented (sequence item as null, mapping value omitted, root as empty text)
Attach a scalar custom tag that constructs a caller-defined value on load and writes that tag back on dump
Attach a sequence custom tag that converts collected items into a different result and dump the tagged sequence; an alias to that node refers to the converted result
Attach a mapping custom tag that receives each pair and dump-then-parse restores the tagged mapping
Register the same tag name for more than one node kind, and prefer an exact tag name over a prefix match
Accept unknown tags through prefix-matching tags and write those tag names back on dump
Refuse a schema without the default string tag, refuse an implicit prefix-matching scalar, fail a recursive alias into a converting tag, and fail a tag that rejects the collected items

Enforce collection nesting depth (omitted default is the implementer’s and is not scored as an exact collection-count pair; aliases are not counted): ten nested flow sequences succeed at 20 and fail at 5; at limit 5, ten aliases to one empty sequence succeed and a recursive self-alias succeeds; 100000 opening brackets fail under the omitted default as a parse failure, not a host stack overflow
Enforce the alias budget per document (default unlimited): two aliases succeed at 2 and fail at 1; budget 0 rejects every alias; two documents that each have one alias succeed at budget 1

Enforce the merge-key budget per parse call (default 10000 keys processed by each `<<` application, shared across a multi-document stream): omitted budget accepts 10000 one-key mappings and rejects 10001; three merged keys succeed at 5 and fail at 2; merging one three-key mapping twice in one `<<` sequence fails at 5 and succeeds at 6; two documents that each merge two keys fail at 3 and succeed at 4; disabling the budget allows a 150-key merge chain
